approach: Walk toward the largest key. If that node has a left subtree, its predecessor is the rightmost key in that subtree; otherwise its parent is the predecessor.
timeComplexity: O(h) time for tree height h.
bankConventions: Keys are distinct. Valid trees have 2..2000 nodes; integer keys fit signed 32 bits.
correctness: A node's predecessor is the largest key in its left subtree, if that subtree exists. Otherwise it is the closest ancestor for which the node lies in the ancestor's right subtree. For the globally largest node this ancestor is its parent, so these cases identify exactly the greatest key remaining after the maximum is excluded.
edgeCases: Two nodes; largest node with a left branch; negative keys; skewed trees.

title: Temperature Tracker
description: Maintain inserted integer temperatures in 0..110. Provide minimum, maximum, arithmetic mean and a most frequent temperature at any time. Getters must not consume readings; any tied mode is valid. Empty-state getters return null.
approach: Keep a fixed 111-entry frequency table, running sum/count and cached extrema/mode. Each insertion updates these constant-size statistics.
timeComplexity: O(1) time per insertion and getter.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space for the fixed domain.
bankConventions: At most 10000 operations; temperatures 0..110. Empty getters return null. Means use relative/absolute tolerance 1e-9; any frequency-maximizing mode is accepted.
correctness: The frequency table counts every insertion. Extrema are updated against every new value; sum/count define the mean; updating the mode on a new largest frequency preserves a maximizing value.
edgeCases: Empty tracker; tied modes; repeated extrema; 0 and 110; interleaved getters.

title: The Cake Thief
description: Each item type has a nonnegative integer weight and nonnegative integer value. Choose any number of whole items of each type with total weight at most a capacity, maximizing total value. Unused capacity is allowed. Preserve the input. A zero-weight positive-value type makes the optimum unbounded, even at capacity zero.
approach: First detect an unbounded zero-weight type. Otherwise compute the best value for each capacity by considering the last positive-weight item selected.
timeComplexity: O(t*C+t+C) time for t types and capacity C, including initialization and zero/empty cases.
bankConventions: 0 <= capacity <= 200; at most 30 types. Weight <= 200 and Value <= 10000000000, with long results fitting signed 64 bits. Infinite optimum is signaled by InfinityException (or corresponding language exception), normalized to {"error":"infinite"}.
correctness: For a bounded instance, an optimal nonempty selection has a final positive-weight item. Removing it leaves a feasible selection at the remaining capacity, so maximizing all such choices establishes the recurrence by induction.
edgeCases: Zero-weight positive value; zero-weight zero value; empty types; zero capacity; values above 32 bits.

title: The Stolen Breakfast Drone
description: An unordered array of positive integers contains one value once and every other value exactly twice. Return the value with one occurrence without changing the array.
approach: XOR all values. Each duplicated value cancels itself, leaving the unmatched one.
bankConventions: 1..10001 entries in 1..2147483647, satisfying the exact multiplicity rule.
correctness: XOR is associative and commutative, and x XOR x is zero. Paired values therefore cancel regardless of ordering, leaving the unique value.
edgeCases: Singleton; large nonconsecutive IDs; unique value at either end.

title: Top Scores
description: Return a new array of the given integer scores in nonincreasing order, preserving all occurrences. Every score is between zero and a supplied maximum K. Preserve the input.
approach: Count occurrences in K+1 buckets, then emit each bucket from K down to zero.
timeComplexity: O(n+K) time, O(n) when K is fixed.
bankConventions: 0 <= K <= 1000; at most 10000 scores, each in 0..K.
correctness: Each input occurrence increments exactly its score bucket. Emitting buckets in decreasing score order preserves multiplicity and produces the required ordering.
edgeCases: Empty input; K=0; repeated scores; unused top bucket.

title: Which Appears Twice
description: An array of length n+1 contains every integer in 1..n exactly once, except one value that occurs twice. Return that duplicated value without changing the array.
approach: XOR all array entries with every integer in 1..n. All required single occurrences cancel, leaving the extra occurrence.
bankConventions: 1 <= n <= 100000. The exact range and multiplicities are guaranteed. The algorithm must avoid overflowing sum formulas.
correctness: Every required integer appears once in each XOR group and cancels. The duplicated integer has one unmatched extra occurrence.
edgeCases: Minimum valid array; duplicate at endpoints of range; large n without sum overflow.

title: Word Cloud Data
description: Count words in a text using the following bank policy: words consist of ASCII letters and may contain an apostrophe or hyphen only when surrounded by letters. Convert every recognized word to lowercase and count all occurrences. Return a dictionary; ordering is irrelevant.
approach: Scan characters once, extending a token through letters and valid internal punctuation. Normalize each completed token to lowercase and increment its dictionary entry.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n text characters.
spaceComplexity: O(n) result storage; one growing dictionary plus the current token.
examplesData: Owls fly; OWLS don't crawl. Fly-by owls!
bankConventions: The source permits several reasonable lexical/capitalization policies. This deterministic ASCII/lowercase policy is an explicit bank convention, not a uniquely mandated source grammar. Input length <= 10000.
correctness: Each maximal sequence satisfying the disclosed token grammar is emitted once. Lowercasing maps permitted case variants to the same dictionary key, and one increment per token gives its occurrence count.
edgeCases: Empty text; mixed case; internal apostrophes/hyphens; repeated punctuation; leading/trailing punctuation.
